neighbours.label: present-state adverbs 'now' / 'already' / 'currently' asserting that something holds at present
fire: Experts warn that the river is now rising faster than last spring.
The vaccine is already available at most pharmacies in the city.
The company is currently hiring engineers for its new office.
Scientists agree that sea ice is now thinner than it was in 1980.
The new law is already changing how landlords set rents.
Tickets for the final are on sale now through the club website.
The species is currently listed as endangered in three countries.
Electric buses are already common on the streets of Shenzhen.
quiet: Experts warn that the river may rise faster than last spring.
The vaccine will be available at most pharmacies next month.
The company plans to hire engineers for its new office.
Scientists measured how thin the sea ice was in 1980.
The new law could change how landlords set rents.
Tickets for the final went on sale last week through the club website.
The species was once listed as endangered in three countries.
Electric buses were rare on the streets of Shenzhen in 2005.

predictions: 'is now', 'is already', 'currently' in explanatory prose fire weakly on the adverb; future or past versions without the adverb stay quiet.
notes: Probe values were low against the 14.1 corpus max: 'is now getting colder' 0.218, 'available now' 0.223, 'Her current contract' 0.098, 'already underway' 0.093 (peak on ' new' instead); future/past controls 0.008-0.078. The median gate of 0.20 will likely fail; recorded as a best guess.
